method: sweep.py scenarios --family <liquid family> (tools/bds-sweep/liquids.py): each cell is laid out on the superflat floor (the floor at y=-1) at `base`; `steps` are the job steps (offsets from `base`; `start` sets a liquid without a block update and a stone on it with one, since BDS leaves a liquid set by a command still until a neighbour changes); in a `timeline` every `watch` position is read once per tick after the tick's events and `trace` keeps [tick, index, block, states] for the first read and each change (the read at tick t shows the world after game tick t - 1). `packets` are the UpdateBlock (`block`) and UpdateSubChunkBlocks (`subchunk`) packets the scripted player was sent in each tick, per entry [dx, dy, dz, layer, flags, block, states] relative to `base`, in packet and entry order.
